walkthroughs.body_html:
Modern Analytical Techniques — a core area of A-Level Chemistry.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Modern Analytical Techniques brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Modern Analytical Techniques.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Which species has the same electron configuration as Ar?
options: Na⁺
Cl⁻
F⁻
Mg²⁺

mcqs.q: Successive ionisation energies of an atom always:
options: Decrease
Stay the same
Increase
Vary randomly

mcqs.q: What are the units of Kc for a reaction?
options: They depend on Δn (the difference between moles of gaseous/aqueous products and reactants) — Kc can be dimensionless or have units like mol dm^-3.
Kc always has units of mol dm^-3.
Kc is always dimensionless.
Standard electrode potentials are measured by submerging the electrode in pure water.

mcqs.q: Why does benzene undergo substitution rather than addition reactions?
options: Benzene cannot react at all because it's too stable.
Standard electrode potentials are measured by submerging the electrode in pure water.
Benzene contains three normal alternating double bonds and behaves like an alkene with three C=C.
Adding across a C=C would destroy the stable delocalised pi system; substitution preserves the aromatic ring.

mcqs.q: Can a single standard electrode potential be measured in isolation?
options: Kc is always dimensionless.
No — electrode potentials are RELATIVE values measured against a reference (the standard hydrogen electrode, defined as 0 V).
Each electrode has an absolute potential that can be measured directly with a voltmeter.
Standard electrode potentials are measured by submerging the electrode in pure water.

Atoms of the same element with the same Z but different numbers of neutrons.
